title: A Server Component imports sibling `lib/` directly, and the client-bundle failure is unreadable without a guard
statement: Under Next.js 16.3.2 with Turbopack, a Server Component imports a Node-only module from a sibling `lib/` directory by plain relative path — no alias, no `transpilePackages`, no bundler configuration — and the value it computes renders in the page. When the same module is reached from a `'use client'` component the build fails either way, but only the `server-only` marker makes the failure locatable: without it Turbopack reports an internal error naming no file and no position; with it the build fails at the marked file's line 1 with the source line and an explanation.

facts.layout: lib/ as a sibling of app/, plain relative import

notes: ⚠️ THE DOCUMENTATION CALLS THE MARKER OPTIONAL, AND FOR THIS PROJECT IT IS NOT. `server-only` changes no runtime behaviour and prevents nothing that was not already prevented — both client imports fail. What it changes is whether the failure is diagnosable, and an unlocatable build error in a tool whose whole premise is legible refusals is the wrong kind of correct. ⚠️ It is the same shape as DEC-0020 and the publisher refusal, arriving a third time: the question is never only whether the wrong thing is stopped, but whether the stop says where.
